groups.title: Controllers & external authority
groups.summary: Phone and MacBook are clients. Existing transport authenticates Groot access; Factory retains work claims and HITL authority.

groups.title: Ordinary .files setup
groups.summary: Reviewed checkout → status and consent → shared modules. Recommended completion never installs K3s.

groups.title: Groot · separately opted-in runtime
groups.summary: Native host → authenticated read-only preflight → explicit server apply → separately applied namespace boundary → bounded CPU Job. Desired architecture, not a deployment receipt.

groups.title: Private evidence boundary
groups.summary: Host observations and retained logs stay outside Git. Checked Bend replay consumes supplied facts; it does not establish their truth.

nodes.title: Phone · Tern / OMP
nodes.summary: OmaLauncher Arch ARM/PRoot runs the existing Tern/OMP controller. Read status and request approved desktop actions; no phone K3s server, sudo or cluster-admin credential copy.

nodes.title: Private access · authenticate
nodes.owner: User · existing Tern / host access policy
nodes.summary: Verify saved desktop identity and host-key pins; preserve working Tern Hosts access. Ordinary SSH requires separately provisioned working authentication and is not established by Tern success. Review Tailscale ACL/netfilter ordering; UFW alone does not prove tailnet isolation.

nodes.title: .files · desired configuration
nodes.summary: Canonical setup contract, shared module code, server defaults and bounded manifests. Verify the actual desktop checkout and reviewed revision; tracked files express intent, not installed state or permission.

nodes.title: Status → consent → selection
nodes.summary: Harness reads status --json and asks before incomplete setup; ./install uses the same onboarding dispatcher. Select modules only after approval, or defer. Recommended complete means core-links + fonts + agent-skills done/done-inferred, not K3s readiness.

citations.symbol: First contact / What recommended setup means

nodes.title: Shared setup modules
nodes.summary: core-links, fonts and agent-skills form the recommended baseline. agent-tools, tailnet-ssh, nix-home and audio-evolution are separately confirmed optional paths. Modules link/install their selected configuration and record local status; none bootstraps K3s.

nodes.title: Groot · native host owner
nodes.owner: User · kvn on native CachyOS desktop
nodes.summary: Native x86_64 systemd/cgroup-v2 host owns service, storage and private admin credentials. Existing Docker/containerd and kind remain independent and untouched, not this K3s runtime. Failures/drift require owner review; start or destructive teardown needs separate explicit approval, backups and workload/network-impact review.

nodes.title: Separate K3s opt-in / preflight
nodes.summary: Distinct K3s opt-in is not onboarding consent. Privileged --check is read-only: native host, root/kubelet/data capacity, assigned private IP, routes, firewall, ports and ownership must pass. Eligibility is not installation; --apply needs explicit approval with the same reviewed flags.

citations.symbol: main / check_host / check_paths / check_network / check_firewall / check_existing

nodes.title: K3s · one private CPU server
nodes.summary: Opt-in v1.36.5+k3s1 server: private API/control plane, local SQLite, bundled containerd/kubelet, built-in scheduler and NetworkPolicy controller. Default server invocation does not select Docker or an external runtime. Traefik/ServiceLB disabled; root-owned kubeconfig stays mode 0600 on Groot. Apply request or ownership marker alone proves no readiness.

nodes.title: oss-factory-jobs · guardrails
nodes.summary: Separately applied restricted-PSA namespace, token-free oss-factory-worker SA with no granted RBAC, worker-guardrail quota (6 nonterminal Pods; 64 Jobs), container LimitRange and default-deny ingress/egress including DNS/API. Object presence is not enforcement evidence, global claim authority or an untrusted-code sandbox.

nodes.title: Bounded CPU Job / smoke
nodes.summary: Quiet namespace and explicit kubectl context; uniquely named fixture/probes only. CPU Job: 1 completion, no retry, 180s deadline, 60s TTL, 500m CPU/256Mi limit, pinned Python image, non-root/restricted security and no credentials/host mounts. No contribution test, worker lease or HITL authorization is created.

nodes.title: Retained results + TTL observation
nodes.owner: External host observer · private local evidence
nodes.summary: Retain source hashes/dirty revision/context, logs, full status and successful results/imageID/node/timing for every captured Pod. Verify live quota AND LimitRange, seventh-Pod denial and independent ingress/egress controls. Matching live TTL plus Job AND dependent-Pod disappearance must be observed without helper deletion. Bounded infrastructure acceptance only, not universal isolation, deployment or Factory approval.

nodes.title: MacBook · client only
nodes.summary: Existing SSH/client access, never server install or cluster join. Optional my.k3sClient.enable defaults false and adds only kubectl/k9s. Prefer host-side commands; native remote kubectl requires separately provisioned scoped RBAC/private transport, never copied desktop cluster-admin credentials.

nodes.title: Factory · claims / HITL authority
nodes.summary: Factory retains global six-worker claims, registry, work orders and upstream-action HITL. Pause submissions through that existing authority for smoke. Namespace quota, manifest claim annotations, smoke receipts and Bend replay cannot issue claims or permissions; no new dispatcher/integration is asserted.

nodes.title: DEFERRED · second agent / GPU
nodes.summary: Not installed or joined by this design. Second PC is a possible later version-compatible CPU agent, never a second standalone server; requires measured need and redesigned inter-node firewall policy. NVIDIA runtime/device plugin and exclusive GPU scheduling require separate compatibility/benchmark approval. No alternate scheduler or GPU fractioning.

scope.title: Phone-controlled .files setup → explicitly opted-in Groot CPU runtime
scope.overview: Existing clients authenticate to Groot; its reviewed .files checkout drives ordinary consent-based modules. A different, explicitly approved preflight/apply path can create one private K3s server, then a separately applied workload boundary and bounded CPU smoke. Private runtime evidence is read from the controller; Factory remains outside this infrastructure's authority.
scope.projection: Four groups and fourteen architectural concepts, not a second state machine. Every existing model state maps exactly once; multiple lifecycle stages highlight the same concept. Nodes with empty states are structural context, not missing lifecycle stages. Recovery states highlight Groot because host-owner review/start/teardown belongs there. Onboarding modules may also target other supported machines; the displayed concrete execution host is Groot.
scope.checkedReplay: Only actual Flow.bend decisions and their existing model-state mapping may determine accepted/refused replay highlights. These structural edges neither grant transitions nor decide policy. A checked transition within one concept stays within that node; no new transition should be inferred from an architectural edge.
scope.edgeStatus: specified means sourced architecture/intent, not installed, running, permitted or replay-accepted. deferred means explicitly excluded from the present single-node CPU design.

externalTrustBoundaries.summary: Existing client/transport identity and authentication must be verified outside Bend; Tern success is not SSH success.
User controller intent does not authenticate root or approve installation. Host admin auth, preflight and scoped apply consent remain separate.
Factory owns global claims, work orders and HITL outside .files/Kubernetes/Bend. This relationship states required external coordination, not an implemented dispatcher or smoke-issued permission.
Execution/enforcement/cleanup facts require real host observation and privately retained evidence. Replay consumes supplied predicates and cannot establish identity, truth, freshness or OS success.

scope.runtimeComponentBasis: K3s runtime grouping follows the pinned default server invocation: no --docker, external container-runtime endpoint, external datastore, alternate scheduler or disabled agent is configured. Existing Docker/containerd/kind on Groot are separate, not reused as K3s components.
nonClaims: No native commands are executed by this JSON or Bend replay.
No K3s installation, SSH success, runtime acceptance, deployment or Factory authorization is claimed.
No Kubernetes quota replaces global worker claims; no Pod security/network-control test proves universal sandbox isolation.
No cluster-admin kubeconfig, token, credential or runtime evidence belongs in Git or on the client.
Second-agent capacity, GPU runtime/device plugin and GPU scheduling remain deferred, not installed.
scope.sourceProvenance: Independently authored .files architecture data with local source citations. No Hapsland source copied or redistributed; topology presentation belongs to the actual upstream renderer, not this data file.
